title: Conjugated comparison isomorphisms and their direct-counit normal form
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_B,\mathcal D_X,\mathcal D_Y,\mathcal D_B$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. Composition is functional, $VU=V\circ U$. Functors preserve identities and composition; natural transformations are families of morphisms with commuting naturality squares, and natural isomorphisms have invertible components. For $h=f,g,c$ use source-target pairs $(X,Y),(Y,B),(X,B)$, respectively. Fix functors $F_h:\mathcal C_s\to\mathcal C_t$, $R_h:\mathcal C_t\to\mathcal C_s$, $P_h:\mathcal D_s\to\mathcal D_t$, $Q_h:\mathcal D_t\to\mathcal D_s$ and $S_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$, and natural isomorphisms
$$\rho_h:S_sR_h\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_hS_t,\quad B_h:S_tF_h\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hS_s,\quad \alpha:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_c,\quad\theta:R_c\xrightarrow{\sim}R_fR_g.$$
Let $\epsilon_c:F_cR_c\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_B}$ be natural and, for each $H\in\mathcal C_B$, let $m_H:P_cQ_cS_BH\to S_BH$ satisfy
$$m_H\circ P_c(\rho_{c,H})\circ B_{c,R_cH}=S_B(\epsilon_{c,H}).$$
The formulas
$$\Xi_H=\rho_{c,H}\circ S_X(\theta_H^{-1})\circ\rho_{f,R_gH}^{-1}\circ Q_f(\rho_{g,H}^{-1}),$$
$$a_G=B_{c,G}\circ S_B(\alpha_G)\circ B_{g,F_fG}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,G}^{-1})$$
define natural isomorphisms $\Xi:Q_fQ_gS_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_cS_B$ and $a:P_gP_fS_X\xrightarrow{\sim}P_cS_X$. For $K=R_cH$ they satisfy
$$\Xi_H^{-1}\circ\rho_{c,H}=Q_f(\rho_{g,H})\circ\rho_{f,R_gH}\circ S_X(\theta_H),$$
and
$$m_H\circ P_c(\rho_{c,H})\circ a_K=S_B(\epsilon_{c,H}\circ\alpha_K)\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$
No adjunction axioms or mate relation between $\alpha$ and $\theta$ are assumed. All compositions of functors use the canonical associators.

proof.text: For natural transformations $u:U\to V$ and $v:V\to W$ and an arrow $x:A\to A'$, naturality twice gives $W(x)\circ v_A\circ u_A=v_{A'}\circ V(x)\circ u_A=v_{A'}\circ u_{A'}\circ U(x)$. For invertible $u$, multiplying $V(x)\circ u_A=u_{A'}\circ U(x)$ by inverses gives $U(x)\circ u_A^{-1}=u_{A'}^{-1}\circ V(x)$. Precomposition replaces $x$ by its functor image; postcomposition applies a functor to the same equality. Finally $T(u_A^{-1})$ is inverse to $T(u_A)$, since their two composites are $T(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. These calculations establish naturality and invertibility of any of the composites below using only the hypotheses and associativity [def-nagata-category].

proof.text:
Apply step 1 to the following chains of natural isomorphisms, with each arrow labelled by its component:
$$Q_fQ_gS_B\xrightarrow{Q_f(\rho_g^{-1})}Q_fS_YR_g\xrightarrow{\rho_{f,R_g(-)}^{-1}}S_XR_fR_g\xrightarrow{S_X(\theta^{-1})}S_XR_c\xrightarrow{\rho_c}Q_cS_B,$$
$$P_gP_fS_X\xrightarrow{P_g(B_f^{-1})}P_gS_YF_f\xrightarrow{B_{g,F_f(-)}^{-1}}S_BF_gF_f\xrightarrow{S_B(\alpha)}S_BF_c\xrightarrow{B_c}P_cS_X.$$
Their components are exactly $\Xi_H$ and $a_G$. Thus both are natural isomorphisms of the claimed functors. Inserting canonical associators changes no component: both bracketings of a functor composite have the same object and arrow action.

proof.text:
Write $r=\rho_{g,H}$, $b=\rho_{f,R_gH}$, $t=\theta_H$, $d=\rho_{c,H}$ and $w=Q_f(r)\circ b\circ S_X(t)\circ d^{-1}$. Reassociating with [def-nagata-category] gives the two inverse products
$$w\circ\Xi_H=Q_f(r)\circ b\circ S_X(t)\circ S_X(t^{-1})\circ b^{-1}\circ Q_f(r^{-1})=\mathrm{id}_{Q_fQ_gS_BH}.$$
$$\Xi_H\circ w=d\circ S_X(t^{-1})\circ b^{-1}\circ Q_f(r^{-1})\circ Q_f(r)\circ b\circ S_X(t)\circ d^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{Q_cS_BH}.$$
Cancel adjacent inverse pairs, using step 1 for functor images. Hence $w=w\circ\Xi_H\circ\Xi_H^{-1}=\Xi_H^{-1}$. Composing on the right with $d$ cancels $d^{-1}\circ d$, giving $\Xi_H^{-1}\circ\rho_{c,H}=Q_f(\rho_{g,H})\circ\rho_{f,R_gH}\circ S_X(\theta_H)$.

source.place: Tag 0014, categories-definition-category; agent calculation from the functor, naturality and invertibility hypotheses of the item.

proof.text:
For $K=R_cH$, expand $a_K$ and reassociate [def-nagata-category]:
$$m_H\circ P_c(\rho_{c,H})\circ a_K=(m_H\circ P_c(\rho_{c,H})\circ B_{c,K})\circ S_B(\alpha_K)\circ B_{g,F_fK}^{-1}\circ P_g(B_{f,K}^{-1}).$$
The parenthesized factor is $S_B(\epsilon_{c,H})$ by the assumed square, since $B_{c,K}=B_{c,R_cH}$. The functor composition law gives $S_B(\epsilon_{c,H})\circ S_B(\alpha_K)=S_B(\epsilon_{c,H}\circ\alpha_K)$. Substituting these two equalities yields the stated direct-counit normal form. No relation between $\alpha$ and $\theta$ enters either calculation.
